newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares seen rangebound before holiday.
newsitem.headline: German shares seen rangebound before holiday.

text.p: German shares struggled slowly to a mixed opening on Wednesday, unmoved by what dealers said were unconvincing records set on Wall Street, and a steady to weaker trend was expected before Thursday's public holiday.
"In many ways we can write off the week already," said a Frankfurt trader.
"Apart from Lufthansa, which is showing some really good volumes this morning, most of the moves seem to be almost accidental," he added.
The IBIS DAX index, which tracks pre-bourse trade, was down 2.97 points at 3,545.55 points at 0721 GMT.
Trading volumes were notably thin, with the exception of Lufthansa, which released news of its first ever quarterly profit overnight. The airline will hold its annual news conference later today.
The stock led trading volumes to rise to a high of 27 marks in early dealings before easing to trade up 11 pfennigs, or 0.4 percent, at 26.60 marks.
"That news was really excellent and is putting some steam behind Lufthansa," a dealer said.
Bayerische Vereinsbank AG started well, then eased back to trade steady after releasing its first quarter results.

The bank reported an 18.7 percent rise in its first quarter operating profit before provisions and said its own-account trading income almost doubled, a fact which dealers said was welcome in the market.
But the overall report was seen as in line with expectations and trading in the bank's shares was not heavy.
Vereinsbank was up six pfennigs at 72.33 marks an hour into trading, off a high of 74 marks.
There were few other highlights in a market muted by the Ascension Day holiday on Thursday, which usually means many investors stay out of the market on Friday as well.
Drugs firm Bayer AG was down 1.6 percent at 67.60 marks after news that it was among four companies to pay the U.S. government $12 million to reimburse health car insurance programmes.
The companies provided blood products that may have resulted in patients acquiring the virus that causes AIDS.
Prices were seen remaining in a fairly tight range, with one bank predicting a range of 3,520 to 3,555 DAX points.
"We won't be testing any key levels, and certainly not on the upside," a trader said.
